reviews.review: This game like all games has those who play for the fun, rewards and points, and others who are just mission interested. When I play this and other team based games I like to gather as many rewards as possible and enjoy playing with others with the same mind set. I would have no issue with recommending this game to others. It reminds me of a pub game I played in my youth called Digger Man, but that was single player with the normal rewards of extra lives when the point scored allowed.

DRG is everything I could want from a game. Fun. Positive community. Humble monetization. I've bought most of the DLC (which is just cosmetics) simply because I want to support the devs for making such a good game. DRG is what gaming is meant to be. ROCK! AND! STONE!

Hands down, Deep Rock Galactic is one of the best co-op games I’ve ever picked up. I’ve already sunk over a thousand hours into it thus far, and regret not writing a review sooner. This is my most played game by quite a bit, and never seems to get old!

First off, the basics. You’re a lowly dwarf employee of the space mining corporation Deep Rock Galactic, set on delving into the depths of the planet Hoxxes IV to exploit the many riches hiding below its surface. However, the native wildlife doesn’t take too kindly to your noisy mining operations. You play as one of 4 classes in a 1-4 person team in an objective based first-person-shooter in a 100% destructible environment.

The build diversity and replayability present are some of the best I’ve seen to date in a game. While every mission may appear similar from the outside, procedural generation, many game-changing modifiers, random encounters and countless other factors make every mission feel refreshingly different. Ignoring stuff like procedural generation, different classes, and build variety, each mission can be one of 9 mission types, with one of 10 secondary objectives, in one of 10 biomes, with 2 of (iirc) 15 warnings or 10 mutators, with over 15 random encounters ranging from giant aggressive plants, to a lost pack from a fallen dwarf, to malfunctioning DRG equipment that must be terminated.

However, I think the part of the game that tickles my fancy the most is the extensive build variety. So many strategies, combos, and techniques arrive from the countless ways you can assemble your loadout and there are so many ways to use all your gear. Every class has a support tool, designed to help the team, a traversal tool, to modify and get around the caves, 4 grenades to choose from, and an armor rig and pickaxe. 3 primary and secondary weapons, each with a 5 tier mod tree each with 2-3 options and an overclock slot fill out each loadout, enabling literally tens of thousands of different options to choose from. Every weapon plays quite differently, and overclocks dramatically change quite a bit of them. I love the strategy of putting together a fun and efficient build and adjusting to a new playstyle every time. It’s what makes the game so replayable in my opinion.

It’s time I talked about the community. The community is so positive and welcoming, perhaps the most wholesome of any game I’ve played to date. While you can play solo, and you’ll get a little robot companion if you do, there’s always a ton of public games you can join at any time, and people are always friendly. I haven’t had a single negative encounter in my 875+ hours of playing, and that’s such a blessing. This game has so much soul, and cooperation is encouraged to the point that you feel this persistent fellowship with the lads. It’s not uncommon to have teammates rushing back to pick up a friend during an extraction, or pinging compressed gold until mission control finally loses it. And then there’s the “Rock and Stone” key, a button dedicated entirely to saluting you and your team. Finish a mission? Rock and Stone. Kill a dreadnought? Rock and Stone. Blow up the scout with a massive block of C4? Rock and Stone. No three words have ever been filled with such passion.

All in all, Deep Rock is such an amazing experience, with friends, randoms, or even just by yourself, I can't wait to sink hundreds more hours into this game!
Beer, bugs, and big, buff blokes, this game has it all. Being excessively inebriated on the job while operating heavy weapons and complex machinery has never been more fun!
Great game, fun, great graphics, no one to play with though
